name: TESSERA PD-5 'Vapor'
description:
A compact chemical defense sprayer the size of a large lipstick tube, dispensing a pressurized stream of synthetic capsaicinoid compound at ranges up to 3 meters. The Vapor delivers an incapacitating chemical agent that causes immediate, severe eye pain, temporary blindness, respiratory distress, and skin irritation lasting 30-45 minutes. The synthetic formulation is 5 times more potent than natural capsaicin and includes a UV-fluorescent dye that marks the attacker's skin for 72 hours, allowing identification by law enforcement.

TESSERA sells the Vapor as the lowest-escalation self-defense option — a chemical deterrent that incapacitates without injury, identifies the attacker for later apprehension, and fits in a pocket or keychain holster. The weapon has become ubiquitous among civilian populations who want protection but are uncomfortable with firearms. At Φ45, it is the cheapest branded defense product in GLMZ.

The Vapor's most significant limitation is its vulnerability to augmentation. Targets with sealed eye protection, respiratory cyberware, or chemical-resistant dermal augmentations are minimally affected. This creates a self-defense gap: the people most likely to threaten civilians — augmented criminals — are the people least affected by the Vapor's payload. The weapon works well against unaugmented attackers, meaning it is most effective against the least dangerous threats.
specifications: range: 3 meters (pressurized stream) effect: Severe eye/respiratory irritation, temporary blindness duration: 30-45 minutes charges: 10 sprays per canister UV dye persistence: 72 hours on skin weight: 30g length: 80mm
tactical_use: Personal defense against unaugmented threats at close range. The Vapor provides an immediately incapacitating effect that creates opportunity to escape. The UV dye assists law enforcement identification. Ineffective against augmented or prepared attackers.
cultural_context: The Vapor is carried by more people in GLMZ than any other defense product — its low cost, small size, and non-lethal classification make it the default choice for anyone who wants some form of protection. 'Vaping someone' has entered slang as a general term for any minor, non-lethal retaliation.
known_users: Anyone who doesn't want to carry a firearm
story_hooks: A batch of Vapor canisters has been found loaded with a compound far more potent than the standard formulation — causing permanent corneal damage instead of temporary irritation. The contaminated canisters are mixed into legitimate retail stock and cannot be identified without chemical analysis.

TESSERA's UV dye database — which logs every Vapor deployment through dye-pattern analysis — has been acquired by a stalking network. The database shows exactly where and when every Vapor was used, providing a map of vulnerable people and their locations.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist cylinder resembling a luxury cosmetic applicator or high-end pen — deceptively elegant for a chemical weapon. The form factor deliberately emphasizes civility and everyday carry. No aggressive angles or tactical aesthetics; instead, smooth curves and a refined silhouette that could pass unnoticed in a pocket or clutched in a closed fist.
physical_description.dimensions: 80mm length × 18mm diameter (lipstick-tube proportions). Thumb-actuator button protrudes 4mm from the rear cap.
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably light — 30g total. Feels insubstantial in the palm, almost fragile. No weight bias; perfectly balanced for one-handed operation. The lightweight nature contrasts sharply with its chemical payload, creating an uncanny sense of concentrated potency in a negligible package.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite with internal pressure vessel (reinforced thermoplastic). The outer shell is injection-molded for seamless finish.
physical_description.finish: Glossy lacquered surface with a subtle pearlescent sheen that catches light without reflecting it harshly. Appears almost opalescent under certain angles — deliberately refined, not tactical. Minimal wear resistance; designed for short operational lifespan before disposal or refill.
physical_description.color_scheme: Soft pearl white primary with discrete charcoal metallic accents around the button mechanism and base cap. A thin band of neon-cyan runs just below the spray nozzle — the only visual identifier of the chemical payload within.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth lacquered polymer with subtle finger-grip indentations molded into the body. The rear cap is wrapped in a thin layer of rubberized coating for secure thumb placement. Intentionally frictionless; designed to slip easily from a pocket or bag.
distinctive_features: Minimalist spray nozzle recessed 2mm into the front, appearing almost like a cosmetic applicator tip rather than a weapon orifice
Thumb-actuator button with soft tactile feedback — requires deliberate pressure to activate, not a hair trigger
Holographic TESSERA logo on the barrel, visible only at certain angles
Serial number etched in micro-print on the base cap
Pressure-release valve visible as a tiny pinhole on the lower side
Neon-cyan accent band — the only visually 'aggressive' element, serving as warning and brand identifier
Transparent polymer section at the top revealing fluid level indicator (appears as a simple line gauge)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA wordmark stamped in matte black on the barrel in minimalist sans-serif typeface. Beneath it: 'PD-5 VAPOR' in smaller letters. Base cap bears the Greek letter Phi (Φ) in micro-print, referencing QUANTA currency and pricing. Manufacturing date code molded into the cap interior.
physical_description.condition_typical: Civilian Vapor devices are typically pristine, stored carefully in pockets or dedicated keychain holsters. Heavy wear is rare — users either fire it in panic and discard/refill it, or keep it sealed. Field examples show minimal cosmetic degradation. Refurbished or tier-5 black-market versions may have scratched lacquer or worn grip sections.
